record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: If X and Y are meager-additive subsets of R, must X × Y be meager-additive? Likewise, if X and Y are null-additive, must X × Y be null-additive?

evidence.quote: Assume that X, Y ⊆ R are meager- (respectively, null-) additive. Does it follow that X × Y is meager- (respectively, null-) additive?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the real line $\mathbb{R}$ with its usual topology and Lebesgue measure. A set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is called:

- meager-additive if for every meager set $M\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, the algebraic sum $X+M=\{x+m:x\in X,\,m\in M\}$ is again meager;
- null-additive if for every Lebesgue null set $N\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, the algebraic sum $X+N$ is again Lebesgue null.

A subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is called meager-additive (respectively null-additive) if the same definition holds with $\mathbb{R}$ replaced by $\mathbb{R}^2$, addition being coordinate-wise, and meagerness (respectively Lebesgue nullness) taken in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Question. Suppose $X,Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}$.

(a) If $X$ and $Y$ are both meager-additive, must the Cartesian product $X\times Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be meager-additive?

(b) If $X$ and $Y$ are both null-additive, must $X\times Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be null-additive?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (Weiss–Zindulka and related literature on sharp measure zero / fractal characterizations of meager-additive sets in $2^\omega$) establishes that in the Cantor space the product of two meager-additive sets is meager-additive, suggesting the meager-additive part has been resolved positively in that setting. The null-additive analogue does not appear to have been settled in the literature consulted, so the problem appears partially solved overall.

status_evidence.title: Strong measure zero and meager-additive sets through the prism of fractal measures
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of meager-additive sets via sharp measure zero; preserved under continuous maps.
status_evidence.claim: Modern fractal-measure characterization of meager-additive sets yields product/closure results in 2^omega.

status_evidence.title: Products of special sets of real numbers (Tsaban–Weiss)
status_evidence.snippet: The product of a meager/null-additive set and a strong measure zero/strongly meager set has strong measure zero/is strongly meager.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work treats products of additive sets with SMZ/strongly meager sets, but does not directly answer the meager- or null-additive product question.
